To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a molecularly imprinted nanoparticle-based biosensor for Hepcidin detection.
we have developed a new method for the detection of Hepcin-25, the iron regulating hormone.
we have developed a novel SPR sensor that is able to detect Hepcidin- 25 at low nanomolar concentration in 3 minutes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new class of MIP NPs for the SPR based detection of the iron hormone Hepcidin.
the development of new tools to improve the detection of iron regulatory hormones in biological fluids.
the design and synthesis of a new generation of molecular recognition elements based on MIP NPs, which can be easily integrated to SPR, and can be used for the development of new biosensors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MIP NP/SPR system is a promising approach to develop an analytical tool for the detection of Hepc-din-25.
the MIP NP based SPR sensor is a promising tool for the determination of Hepcidein-25 in biological fluids and in the development of new diagnostic assays for iron dis-metabolistis and doping.
the MIP NP SPR sensor is a promising tool for the detection of Hepacidin-25.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MIP NPs can be used as recognition elements in SPR for the detection of low molecular weight compounds.
the combination of SPR and MIP NP is a powerful approach for the development of new sensors for the detection of small molecules in biological fluids.
MIP NPs could be integrated to SPR for the detection of small analytes at very low concentrations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
MIP NP are a powerful tool for SPR biosensing.
the integration of MIP NPs in SPR allows the determination of the target analyte at very low concentrations in a short time.
MIP NPs can be integrated to a SPR sensor to achieve the detection of the analyte in a very fast time, with a high selectivity and sensitivity.
